characters: Bempong: an eight-year-old Ghanaian boy with short neat hair in a yellow shirt and khaki-brown shorts school uniform, holding a clear cup.
Fiati: his eight-year-old Ghanaian girl classmate with neat braided hair in a yellow shirt and brown pinafore school uniform, holding a plain unlabelled sketchbook.
Their teacher: a warm Ghanaian female teacher in a bright green-and-gold patterned dress beside a classroom window shelf.

narrationPlan.voice: A patient boy’s voice for Bempong; a bright girl’s voice for Fiati
narrationPlan.pace: Patient, with a pause for each day (about 90 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with a different voice for each character.
Pause for two seconds at each question activity.
Never rush the last page: let the ending land.

music: A slow, soft tune with a light rising note for each day (placeholder)
culturalNotes: Maize and beans are common crops across Ghana, and many children see farmers plant them at the start of the rains. The story follows the NaCCA Science standards on the life cycle of plants and the germination of maize and bean seeds (B1.2.2.1, B3.2.2.1.2).
A bean seed splits into two halves; a maize seed has one. The story states this simply and checks are listed for reviewers.
reviewQuestions: Is the language right for the stated age band and reading level?
Is anything here inaccurate, stereotyped or unsafe for children?
Check the germination steps (water, air and warmth; the root first, then the shoot) against NaCCA B3.2.2.1.2.
Check that the story does not give a fixed number of days, because germination time depends on the seed and the weather.

teacherGuide.overview: A cup-and-cloth experiment shows a bean seed sprouting. Children learn what a seed needs, the order of root, shoot and leaves, and how a bean differs from maize. Based on NaCCA Science standards on the plant life cycle and germination.
learningGoals: Say what a seed needs to sprout.
Put the stages of germination in order.
Say how a bean and maize seed differ.

subjectLinks.subject: Science (NaCCA B1.2.2.1, B3.2.2.1.2)
subjectLinks.link: Life cycle of a plant and germination

beforeReading: Ask: what is inside a seed? What does it need?
whileReading: Look at the cup together each day and draw what you see.
afterReading: Compare seeds in two cups, one wet and one dry, and say what happened.
Plant a sprouted seed in the school garden.
discussion: Why must we keep the cloth wet?
What will the plant need next?
reflection: How did it feel to wait for the seed?

support: Use pictures of four stages and put them in order.
stretch: Compare how fast maize and beans sprout.

culturalNotes: Maize and beans are common crops across Ghana, and many children see farmers plant them at the start of the rains. The story follows the NaCCA Science standards on the life cycle of plants and the germination of maize and bean seeds (B1.2.2.1, B3.2.2.1.2).
A bean seed splits into two halves; a maize seed has one. The story states this simply and checks are listed for reviewers.
localiseThis: Use the beans, cowpea or maize seed your school can get.
Wash hands after touching soil and seeds. Never eat seeds that have been treated for planting.
